gen-fs-nippo-gf-cascadia-mono: Technical right away, since Nippo makes its small letters nearly capital-sized. Nippo is best at wire-cut display shapes, while Cascadia Mono does its best work lining up compact letters like pins in a wide board.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-chivo: Chivo packs its lowercase up toward the caps and lets daylight through every curve, while Nippo bends uniform strokes like cable. Nudge Chivo up a size and the body text settles in.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-comme: Comme draws smooth curves that never clog, with lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height. And once the text runs on, it glides along smoothly, a quiet follow-up to the wire-like Nippo.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-cossette-texte: Wire-cut and proud, Nippo leads while Cossette Texte sits below with a prominent x-height and wide-eyed e. Text in plain sans runs smoothly, each arch sturdy as its stems.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-funnel-sans: Clean throughout, Funnel Sans holds its stroke widths steady from stem to curve. Next to Nippo, those tiny ascender gaps and pried-open e feel quietly precise against the wire-cut display letters.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-gafata: Gafata reads tall and open, with a deep band of lowercase. Nippo, with no stroke contrast at all, supplies the wire-cut punch while Gafata adds a touch of low contrast beneath it.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-vadodara: Sharp little wire-cut letters up top, big open-looking ones underneath. Nippo brings the technical edge, and Hind Vadodara supplies spacious terminal gaps and tall bowls so each line holds together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-giga: Wire-cut and widely spaced: Nippo stands proud with nearly capital-sized small letters, while Lexend Giga lays out flat, single-weight lines. What holds them together is a shared, modern technical streak.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-tera: Contemporary through and through, Lexend Tera draws like a plotter pen. Nippo adds wire-cut display punch with proud small letters, and the stepping-stone spacing below gives each line room to breathe.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable and widely tracked, Lexend Zetta lays down ribbon-like strokes of constant width beneath the wire-cut Nippo. Both draw with one steady line, and that is what unites them.
